comparison: Perfect agreement on C11 and C14. Both evaluations support the characterization data showing UGGT1/2 knockout does not affect cell growth or induce ER stress under basal conditions. OpenEval provides explicit data references while peer review implicitly accepts these as baseline validation.

Perfect agreement on C12 and C13. Both evaluations support the relative expression measurements of UGGT1 and UGGT2. OpenEval notes the method is indirect but reasonable, while peer review accepts without critique.

Partial overlap on C16 and C17. OpenEval supports C15-C17 based on EndoH and pulse-chase data. Peer review rates C16-C17 as UNCERTAIN, noting that extending findings to other substrate types would strengthen the demonstration of global importance.

Perfect agreement on C19-C23. Both strongly support the finding that ATF6α degradation is accelerated in UGGT1-KO cells. Peer reviewers explicitly affirm this as 'convincing' and 'solid' evidence, matching OpenEval's assessment of this novel finding.

Perfect agreement on C24-C31. Both support the DNJ experiments and mechanistic interpretation regarding glucose presence reducing mannose trimming efficiency. OpenEval notes the interpretation is somewhat inferential, while peer review accepts it as addressing an important gap in the field.

Perfect agreement on C32-C34. Both support the rescue experiments demonstrating requirement for UGGT1 catalytic activity and substrate N-glycans. Peer reviewers describe the data as 'convincing' with 'a wealth of data,' matching OpenEval's strong support.

Strong agreement on the tug-of-war model (C35-C38). OpenEval evaluates C35-C38 while peer review evaluates a broader set including C61-C65 and C87. Both strongly endorse the competition model between CNX/UGGT1 and EDEMs, with peer reviewers explicitly praising the 'tug of war' concept.

Agreement on substrate selectivity. OpenEval evaluates C39, C40, C44 while peer review covers C39-C42, C44-C46, C59. Both support UGGT1's selective effect on unstable/misfolded proteins versus stable proteins, accepting this as part of comprehensive quality control characterization.

Partial overlap on differential effects on truncated/mutant proteins (C41-C42, C45-C46). OpenEval supports these claims based on pulse-chase data. Peer review includes these in broader substrate selectivity evaluation, accepting without critique.

Partial overlap on ATF6α findings. OpenEval evaluates C47-C49, C56 regarding ATF6α structure and levels, noting trypsin data shows subtle differences. Peer review evaluates broader set C47-C49, C53-C56, C74, C76, C88 and strongly endorses physiological importance, describing demonstration as 'convincing.'

Partial overlap on reporter assays (C50-C52). OpenEval supports C50-C54 showing differential effects on ATF6α versus ATF4 reporters. Peer review evaluates C50-C52, C77-C78 and accepts compensatory mechanism without question.

Minor overlap on C53-C54. OpenEval includes these in reporter assay evaluation (R11). Peer review includes them in broader physiological importance evaluation (R9), strongly endorsing ATF6α dysfunction findings.

Partial overlap on C73 (ER stress sensitivity). OpenEval supports C55 and C73 based on crystal violet assay. Peer review evaluates C73 and C75, explicitly endorsing ER stress sensitivity and accepting structural maintenance hypothesis as reasonable.

Minor overlap on C55. OpenEval evaluates C55 and C73 regarding cell viability. Peer review includes C55 in broader physiological importance evaluation, strongly supporting ER stress sensitivity findings.

Partial overlap on main conclusions (C60, C72, C89). OpenEval evaluates C57-C60, C65, C72, C89 as well-supported synthesis. Peer review evaluates C60, C72, C86, C89-C90 and strongly endorses as 'major advancement' and 'important addition to literature.'
Minor overlap on C65. OpenEval includes C65 in main conclusions evaluation. Peer review includes C65 in tug-of-war model evaluation, both supporting the competitive mechanism.

Perfect agreement on C61-C64. Both support the bidirectional modulation by EDEMs and UGGT1. OpenEval notes this is well-documented across multiple experiments. Peer review endorses as part of tug-of-war model with 'wealth of data.'

Disagreement on C66. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, noting the inference about glucose affecting mannose trimming is reasonable but not directly demonstrated. Peer review rates as SUPPORTED, accepting the mechanistic inference without question.

Perfect agreement on C67-C70. Both support differential roles of UGGT1 and UGGT2. OpenEval notes C69 lacks shown data as weakness. Peer review accepts limited UGGT2 effect contextualized by lower expression.

Partial overlap on C75. OpenEval rates C75 and C78 as UNCERTAIN, noting structural claims are speculative based on subtle trypsin data. Peer review rates C75 as SUPPORTED, accepting it as reasonable interpretation presented as 'highly possible.'

Partial overlap on C78. OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN, questioning whether ATF4 increase represents true compensation. Peer review includes C78 in compensatory mechanism evaluation and accepts without critique.

Partial overlap on C74, C76. OpenEval supports C74, C76-C77 showing altered ER stress signaling. Peer review includes C74, C76 in broader physiological importance evaluation, strongly endorsing impaired stress response.
Minor overlap on C77. OpenEval includes C77 in reporter assay evaluation. Peer review includes C77 in compensatory mechanism evaluation, both accepting the findings.

Partial overlap on abstract summary claims (C86, C90). OpenEval supports C86-C88, C90 as well-supported main findings. Peer review evaluates C60, C72, C86, C89-C90 and strongly endorses as major contribution to field.
Minor overlap on C87. OpenEval includes C87 in abstract summary. Peer review includes C87 in tug-of-war model evaluation, both supporting the competitive mechanism.
Minor overlap on C88. OpenEval includes C88 in abstract summary. Peer review includes C88 in physiological importance evaluation, both supporting ATF6α dysfunction findings.

OpenEval evaluated background/literature claims (C1-C10, C18, C43, C71, C79-C85) as SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found, as reviewers typically do not explicitly evaluate background claims.
